questions.question: What does the geometric distribution used in this course count?
options: Successes in a fixed number of trials
Successes in a sample without replacement
A continuous value on an interval

options: A continuous density on an interval
Equal masses on a finite support

questions.question: For independent fair coin tosses, the number of tails before the first head has which distribution?

How is the geometric failure count related to independent Bernoulli trials?
options: It counts successes among a fixed number of trials

questions.question: Why is the exponent $k$ in the zero-based PMF $(1-p)^kp$?
options: There are $k$ successes before the first failure
There are $k$ failures before the next trial succeeds
The first success must occur on trial $k$
The failures may be placed anywhere among fixed trials

questions.question: How do geometric failure counts differ from binomial success counts?
options: Geometric trials deplete a population; binomial values are continuous
Geometric stops at success; binomial fixes the trial count
Geometric counts have a fixed bound; binomial counts do not
The two counts always have the same distribution

At $p=0$, the first success occurs immediately

questions.question: How does the geometric failure count relate to the trial-count negative binomial variable $N$?
options: For one required success, it is $N-1$
It is always a Poisson count
It is a continuous version of $N$
